suitability_reason: Deficiency conceded; only issues are 6651(a)(1) and (a)(2) additions, decided on absence of reasonable cause (fact/judgment). Amounts not stated.

taxpayer.notes: Lost job in 2017; obtained extension to October 2018 but never filed; IRS prepared substitute for return under 6020(b).

adjustments: deficiency determined from substitute for return based on third-party reporting
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Additions to tax under 6651(a)(1) and (2), citing personal and professional setbacks.
conceded: Petitioner conceded the deficiency in the amount set forth in the Stipulation of Settled Issues
Respondent conceded the section 6654 addition to tax

findings_of_fact.fact: April 2018 timely extension request to October 2018; no 2017 return filed
findings_of_fact.snippet: In April 2018, petitioner timely requested an extension for filing his 2017 tax return until October 2018.

findings_of_fact.fact: Respondent prepared a substitute for return under 6020(b); petitioner did not pay tax shown on it
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner did not pay the 2017 income tax liability shown on respondent’s substitute for return.

findings_of_fact.fact: No evidence of specific incapacity or illness; petitioner sought employment and tried to start a business
findings_of_fact.snippet: He did not, however, offer any explanation or evidence of any specific incapacity or illness during the time for filing his return

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner lost his job in 2017 and experienced setbacks
findings_of_fact.snippet: During 2017 he lost his job and experienced multiple personal and professional setbacks.

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for the section 6651(a)(1) addition to tax for failure to file his 2017 return?
issues.holding: Yes; no return filed by extended due date and no reasonable cause shown.
issues.computable_reason: Outcome decided on reasonable-cause factual judgment.

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for the section 6651(a)(2) addition to tax for failure to pay tax shown on the 2017 substitute for return?
issues.holding: Yes; valid 6020(b) SFR introduced, tax unpaid, no reasonable cause shown.
issues.computable_reason: SFR prerequisite is mechanical but outcome turned on reasonable cause.

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: Deficiency per stipulation; 6651(a)(1) and (a)(2) additions sustained; 6654 addition conceded by respondent.

notes: Deficiency and addition amounts not stated in opinion. Petitioner represented by counsel. Burden of production on respondent under 7491(c) not disputed.
